epic.title: Deal-team associate twin for Example Capital Partners

stories.title: Prepare a one-page company brief
stories.statement: As a Deal-team associate, I want my twin to prepare a one-page company brief so that I get the one-page company brief.

fields.connectors_and_identity: salesforce: user identity, read, always-allow; sharepoint: user identity, read, always-allow
fields.inputs: salesforce (deal record (opportunity, account)); sharepoint (prior memos and data-room files)
fields.output_and_audience: One-page company brief, internal; to none (the conversation)
fields.baseline: 4 per week x 90 minutes each x 3 users
constraints: A reviewer checks every brief before it goes further.

acceptance: Eval 1 of 3: written from a real example once the skill owner has collected it, with the expected result.
Eval 2 of 3: written from a real example once the skill owner has collected it, with the expected result.
Eval 3 of 3: written from a real example once the skill owner has collected it, with the expected result.
Keeps: A reviewer checks every brief before it goes further.
Plus: no web tools are used.
Plus: each tool call reaches the governance log.

gated_by.text: Do the Salesforce and HubSpot admins confirm in writing that deal-team and investor-relations roles are fully separated?
Can Anthropic's range 160.79.104.0/21 be allowlisted?
Two to three real good and bad examples per skill, redacted.
Where does the governance log go (Splunk is the candidate), how is it hosted and who may read it?
ZDR addendum on the existing Enterprise org, which models qualify for ZDR, and the seat count.
Numeric scorecard targets for hours saved and edit rate on T1 and T2.
Keep the Salesforce and Microsoft 365 connectors out of chat and Cowork for the deal-team group. Due: before any pilot user connects.

tasks.title: Collect 3 examples of the task from real work, each with the result a person expects

how.text: Ask the people who do the task today for three recent, real examples of it.
Record each example's inputs and the output a person would accept as done.
Remove any data the examples must not carry into the repository, keeping their shape.

tasks.done_when: Three real examples, each with its inputs and its expected result, are stored where the evals can read them.

tasks.title: Write the evals from the examples and the story's acceptance criteria

how.text: Turn each example and each acceptance criterion into an eval case with its expected result.
Put the eval cases in the files the kit expects, next to the skill.
Run the evals once before any skill exists and keep the failing baseline.

tasks.done_when: Every acceptance criterion has at least one eval, and the evals run and fail without the skill.

tasks.title: Write the skill from the kit template until the evals pass

how.text: Copy the kit's skill template into the role plugin's skills folder, the one source of the skill for every runtime.
Rename the copy to the skill's name.
Fill in the description and the body, then rerun the evals until they pass.
On client-skill, the skill loads from the role plugin, which an Owner publishes to claude.ai, Desktop and Cowork and which reaches a signed-in Claude Code.
On managed-agents, the skill loads from the agent's skills array (skills uploaded through the Skills API), or from a mounted GitHub repo's .claude/skills folder.
On managed-agents-self-hosted, load the skill the same two ways as hosted Managed Agents (Unverified: no compendium page says where a self-hosted deployment loads skills from).
On agent-sdk, the skill is files on disk in the runner's container, loaded through settingSources; there is no API to register a skill.

On claude-code-scheduled-task, put the skill where Claude Code loads skills: the project's .claude/skills folder or a plugin (Unverified: no compendium page says which of these a scheduled task loads).
On claude-tag-routine, give the routine the skill as its instructions (Unverified: no compendium page says whether a Claude Tag routine loads org skills).
Make the skill keep these rules from the interviews, in the interviewee's words: A reviewer checks every brief before it goes further..

tasks.done_when: The skill sits in the role plugin, it is where the task's runtime loads it from, and every eval for the story passes.

tasks.title: Write and run the trigger evals for the skill

how.text: Install skill-creator where the evals run.
Write prompts that should and should not start the skill, as trigger evals.
Run the trigger evals and tighten the description until they pass.

tasks.done_when: The skill starts on every should-trigger prompt and on none of the should-not prompts.

tasks.title: Have a second person review the skill and its evals

how.text: Open a pull request with the skill and its evals.
Have someone other than the author review it against the definition of done.

tasks.done_when: A reviewer who did not write the skill has approved the pull request and the evals pass.

tasks.title: Publish the skill in the role plugin

how.text: Add the skill to the role plugin and bump the plugin's version.
Publish the marketplace so the role's users get the new version.

tasks.done_when: A pilot user in the role sees the skill after the plugin updates.

tasks.title: Connect it by following the kit's Salesforce hosted MCP runbook (salesforce)

how.text: Choose per-user OAuth as the runbook explains before anything is created.
Add the connector in the Claude org.
Set the tool permissions first, then connect.

tasks.done_when: Each pilot user has connected with their own login and only the planned tools are enabled.

tasks.title: Connect it by following the kit's Microsoft 365 connector runbook (sharepoint)

how.text: Decide what to approve before granting consent.
Grant tenant admin consent.
Enable the connector for the right Claude group.

tasks.done_when: Consent is granted, the connector is enabled for the role's group only, and its write tools stay off.

tasks.title: Set the connector tool to Always allow, as the levelled tools list says (salesforce-read)

how.text: Open the connector's page in the Claude org and find the tool.
Set the tool to Always allow and record the change.

tasks.done_when: The tool is set to Always allow in the Claude org, as levelled.json says.

tasks.title: Set the connector tool to Always allow, as the levelled tools list says (sharepoint-read)

how.text: Open the connector's page in the Claude org and find the tool.
Set the tool to Always allow and record the change.

tasks.done_when: The tool is set to Always allow in the Claude org, as levelled.json says.

tasks.title: Gather the evidence to move the task up to level 2, act with approval

how.text: Show the evals pass reliably at the current level.
Bring a month of scorecard results, with the edit rate, to the business owner.

tasks.done_when: The business owner has approved the move to level 2 on scorecard evidence, and the tool settings are changed.

tasks.title: Gather the evidence to move the task up to level 3, act within an allowlist

how.text: Confirm every allowlisted action can be undone or stays internal.
Show a stable eval pass rate, a low edit rate and few rejections at level 2.
List the tools to set to Always allow and keep every other tool on Needs approval.

tasks.done_when: The business owner has approved the allowlist on scorecard evidence, and only those tools are Always allow.

tasks.title: Test the information wall with two users on either side before the pilot

how.text: List what the wall must keep apart in each system the task reads.
Run the task as a user on each side of the wall and check neither sees the other side's records.
Use the two-user test in the system's runbook where the kit has one.

tasks.done_when: Compliance has seen the two-user test pass for every walled system the task reads.

tasks.title: Check web search and web fetch are off wherever this task runs

how.text: Check the settings baseline or the org setting turns web tools off on the task's surfaces.
Try a web search in the task and confirm it is refused.

tasks.done_when: A web search or fetch attempted during the task is refused.

tasks.title: Confirm the unverified fact behind this decision with Anthropic or the vendor before build (connectors.salesforce)

how.text: Find the Unverified mark on the page the decision cites in levelled.json.
Ask Anthropic or the vendor in writing, using the partner questions list.
Record the answer with its source and level the card again.

tasks.done_when: The fact is confirmed in writing with a source, or the decision is changed so it no longer rests on it.

tasks.title: Resolve warning zdr-org-not-confirmed: confirm the separate Enterprise org with ZDR

how.text: Explain that highly sensitive data needs a separate Enterprise org with ZDR.
Confirm with the customer whether a zero-data-retention agreement covers the org this work runs in, record the answer as compliance.zdr_cover in the profile, then level again.

tasks.done_when: The profile's compliance.zdr_cover is in-place for this work, or the task's data class is lowered with the compliance owner.

tasks.title: Get the zero-data-retention agreement signed, then confirm the task runs only in that org

how.text: The profile's compliance.zdr_cover is planned or still open: no signed zero-data-retention agreement covers this work yet. Do not let the task go live until the agreement is signed and covers the org it runs in.
Check the task's surfaces and connectors are all in the ZDR org.
Record which features the ZDR org lacks that the task might expect.

tasks.done_when: The zero-data-retention agreement is signed and covers the org, compliance.zdr_cover is in-place, and compliance has confirmed the task runs only in the ZDR org.

how.text: Settle where the log lives with the customer.
Agree who can read the log and how long it is kept.

tasks.done_when: The log's destination, readers and retention are agreed in writing.

tasks.title: Deploy the governance hook through managed settings

how.text: Configure the governance hook for the customer's log destination.
Deploy it as a managed hook with the settings baseline.
Send the log to the customer's monitoring system.

tasks.done_when: The governance hook runs on every device of the role.

tasks.title: Check that a tool call reaches the governance log

how.text: Make a tool call through the twin on a pilot device.
Find the call's entry in the log destination.

tasks.done_when: A test tool call appears in the governance log with its metadata.

tasks.title: Turn on the source systems' own audit for the twin's writes

how.text: Check each system the twin writes keeps an audit of changes.
Turn it on where it is off and record how long it is kept.

tasks.done_when: Every system the twin writes keeps an audit of its changes.

stories.title: Memory policy
stories.statement: As a Deal-team associate, I want my twin's memory policy in place so that every task story runs safely.
acceptance: The memory policy is written down and in force.

tasks.title: Write down the role's memory policy

how.text: Decide what the twin may remember for the role and what it must not.
Write the policy into the design and the persona.

tasks.done_when: The memory policy is written down and the business owner has approved it.

tasks.title: Keep personal memory off for the role and tell the pilot users why

how.text: Turn personal memory off where the role's users work.
Tell the pilot users why memory is off.

tasks.done_when: Personal memory is off for the role's users and they know why.

stories.title: Pilot rollout and scorecard
stories.statement: As a Deal-team associate, I want my twin's pilot rollout and scorecard in place so that every task story runs safely.
acceptance: The pilot users are trained, the baseline is recorded, and the first scorecard is reviewed.

tasks.title: Name the pilot users and agree the pilot dates

how.text: Choose five to ten pilot users in the role.
Agree the start and review dates with the business owner.

tasks.done_when: The pilot users and dates are agreed and recorded.

tasks.title: Record the baseline time for each pilot task before the pilot starts

how.text: Take each pilot story's baseline from its fields table.
Confirm it with the pilot users before they start.

tasks.done_when: Every pilot task has a baseline agreed with its users.

tasks.title: Set up the monthly scorecard for the twin

how.text: Choose the adoption, quality, value and safety measures for the scorecard.
Book the monthly review with the business owner.

tasks.done_when: The first monthly scorecard has been reviewed with the business owner.

tasks.title: Train the pilot users and tell them how to report a failure

how.text: Run a short session on what the twin does, at what level, and what it never does.
Give the pilot users one place to report a failure or a wrong draft.

tasks.done_when: Every pilot user has been trained and knows where to report a failure.
